intro: Lesson 16: Cyber security: threats and how to stay safe. Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

passage.title: From: Security Team <support@bank-secure-alerts.co>
paras: Subject: URGENT: Your account will be closed in 24 hours
We have detected unusual activity on your acount. To keep your money safe, you must verify your details immediately or your account will be closed.
Please enter your full card number, PIN and password.

questions.q: Find five warning signs in the email.
questions.a: Urgent threat (24 hours); generic greeting (Dear Customer); spelling mistakes (acount, Securty); a strange sender address and link; asks for PIN and password (banks never do)

questions.q: What should you do with an email like this?
questions.a: Do not click or reply; report it (for example forward to report@phishing.gov.uk) and delete it; contact the bank using its official number.

questions.q: Find three phishing signs in the teacher's example email.
questions.a: Odd sender address, urgency, a request for login details.

questions.q: Make a one-page cyber security guide for your family (five tips with reasons) in the HTML editor or a document; save to the portal.
Extend: explain what ransomware is and why backups help.
questions.a: It locks files for a payment; backups let you restore without paying.

questions.q: Which is a sign of phishing?
options: It asks for your password urgently
It's from your teacher about a lesson
questions.a: A) It asks for your password urgently. Real services never ask for passwords like that.

questions.q: Think again: A message says 'Your account will be closed! Click here now!' What should make you suspicious?
questions.a: Urgency, a threat, and a link: classic phishing signs.
